A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide complete, readable main text and Appendices A-B. Their equations, algorithms, figures, and tables can be matched reliably despite local edits and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-function and language-model experiments measuring approximation errors, demonstration-selection performance, and computational costs, with additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in the main text and appendices, including benchmark evaluations, ablations, and Hessian measurements.

M1.justification: Gradient estimation, anchor averaging, and the random-ensemble, forward-selection, and cross-entropy variants are retained. Algorithm 2 clarifies anchor-specific estimates and demonstration membership without changing the procedure already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both retain the six main sentiment/reasoning datasets, synthetic function studies, and appendix evaluations on Snarks, Sports Understanding, and StrategyQA. Nonlinear functions were already evaluated in v1; the revised Figure 2 caption does not establish added coverage.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains random-k, BM25, top-k, UR, BRIDGE, and top-k + CE. The full-inference comparisons and comparator membership in the corresponding synthetic experiments and appendix tables are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The models, query counts, metrics, and selection settings are retained, including projection dimension 400. The concrete linear-function selection experiment still uses three coefficient vectors in 20 dimensions; removing a general restriction does not document a changed tested configuration.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 and Appendices B.3-B.5 retain the same sensitivity, duplicate-sample, demonstration-order, label-choice, and Hessian/generalization analyses. No analysis or supporting experimental evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds and standard deviations for Table 4, and 30 random seeds and standard deviations for Table 12. Uncertainty reporting elsewhere is also retained without changed run counts or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted results are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 4 retains ICL-GRADRE scores of 91.6±1.8 on SST-2 and 75.2±3.7 on Coin Flip, while Table 3 retains the maximum 37.7× speedup.

T1.justification: Section 3 removes the restriction C < d on the number of coefficient vectors in the synthetic linear-function setup, relaxing a stated assumption. Other dimension edits are notational; the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma and Hessian derivation in the appendices are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same gradient-estimation and linear-time selection contributions, together with the same headline approximation-error, speedup, and performance claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of ensemble scoring, label insensitivity, and generalization are retained. The limitations concerning out-of-distribution robustness and more principled anchor selection also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 now explicitly describes independent Gaussian matrix entries, but that construction was already documented in v1's Appendix A.3. Hyperparameters, hardware and runtime details, dataset/model sources, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are unchanged. Removing the introductory retrieval-problem phrase before the discussion of Yu et al. (2025) leaves its account of retrieval ranking and the paper's novelty claims intact.

P1.justification: Local clarifications define embedding dimension p, distinguish it from projection dimension d, clarify k as the number of selected examples, and improve Algorithm 2's notation. A few sentences are edited, while the section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1's spacing is adjusted, Figure 2's caption changes 'noisy linear regression' to 'nonlinear regression,' and Figure 3 moves from page 7 to page 8. Expanded pseudocode causes local reflow; all figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity by distinguishing dimensions, clarifying k, and making Algorithm 2's anchor-specific estimates and sample membership explicit. These refinements make the existing procedure easier to follow without strengthening its empirical evidence. Figure 2's revised caption agrees with its nonlinear legend, although Section 3's noisy-linear description remains inconsistent.
